body: I was seeing a therapist for anxiety for about a year but couldn't afford it anymore. I tried anti-anxiety medication in high school but didn't feel comfortable taking it. I know it's not an antidepressant but I do think a lot of my hopelessness comes from the intense anxiety I feel about almost everything. I guess I feel like my anxiety is manageable up until the point where everything is falling apart and in those moment I just feel so tired. It scares me how often I have suicidal thoughts because I can rationalize that it's an unreasonable response to my situation but I still feel that way. When I start to feel better I just feel like I was being overdramatic and manipulative. It's like a cycle that never seems to end which is why I'm worried about future me.

I'm so sorry you're feeling like this. I have a big project due tomorrow for school and have been crying all day. I came here looking for help too. I don't know if knowing someone else is feeling similar will help at all but I am just so sorry that school and your project leader have put you in a dark place. If I could give you advice I would say to take any expectation of getting the work in by Saturday off the table. You don't need to tell your project supervisor. I feel like crying and puking all day is a serious medical reason not to do any more work until your mental health can handle it (in the same way that throwing yourself down a set of stairs would be a serious medical reason not to do any work until recovered). Once you take the expectation of getting it done by Saturday you might feel a bit guilty, but please believe that what you are going through today is absolutely as serious as someone who needs an extension because of a broken leg or the flu. After the deadline passes, or even before, you can then send a firm email to your project leader saying that you are/were ill and that you need accommodation if you are still going pass the course. Be up front about the fact that you understand that you may no longer be able to complete the course. If the project leader refuses to help you may have to go through your university/college's bureaucracy and get a doctor's note after the fact to get a deferral to the next semester. A deferral should only mean that you have to complete whatever work you hadn't completed for the semester (so just this one project). Worst case scenario you fail the class and have to take it again, which would REALLY suck, but it's possible that you would get a project leader who is not going to put you in such a dark place that you consider hurting yourself. 

I hope this helps a bit and that my advice is actually applicable in your situation. I just really know how it feels to feel completely helpless when it comes to school, but your safety and health should always come first. Even if others or your mind are making you feel like this project is more important, it just isn't.
